EL1001.fix: Remove the byte order mark at the start of the file. Preview edilint fix before using --write; fix removes a UTF-8 BOM.
EL1001.false_positives: Some delimited-file consumers accept a BOM from spreadsheet exports, so this rule is a warning for that format. Confirm the receiver's encoding contract before suppressing it.

EL1002.example: A text field contains the standalone byte 0xFF, which is not a valid UTF-8 sequence.
EL1002.fix: Decode the file using its actual source encoding and export valid UTF-8, or regenerate it from the source. Do not replace undecodable bytes blindly; the original value may be lost.
EL1002.false_positives: A feed intentionally encoded in a legacy character set can trigger this rule. Convert it according to the agreed encoding before linting. Dense binary input is reported once and is not parsed as an interchange.

EL1003.fix: Remove the unintended control byte in the exporting system. Preserve declared field and record separators. Check whether tabs came from spreadsheet or copy-and-paste processing.
EL1003.false_positives: Tabs in record content are warnings. A nonstandard feed may intentionally carry control bytes; suppress the rule only when the consumer explicitly accepts them. Declared separators are exempt.

EL1004.example: An identifier reads ACME but contains AC\u200BME (a zero-width space).
EL1004.fix: Regenerate the identifier without the formatting character. Inspect the source bytes, since the character may be invisible in the editor.
EL1004.false_positives: Bidirectional formatting can be intentional in free text. Check the field's purpose and receiver support before removing it; an identifier should be reviewed separately from prose.

EL1005.example: N1*PR*АCME~  (the first letter is Cyrillic U+0410, not Latin A)
EL1005.fix: Confirm the intended value with the source. For accidental lookalikes, preview edilint fix --unsafe, which proposes substitutions; inspect the diff before adding --write.
EL1005.false_positives: A legitimate name in another alphabet may contain a character resembling an ASCII letter. Do not transliterate names merely to clear a warning. The unsafe fix tier requires deliberate review.

EL1006.fix: Confirm the feed's allowed character set. If it requires ASCII, correct the export using an agreed transliteration policy rather than silently dropping characters.
EL1006.false_positives: Unicode names and free text may be intentional. This is a warning for review; an agreed Unicode feed can disable or downgrade it.

EL1007.example: With --charset basic: N1*PR*Acme~  (lowercase letters are outside the basic profile)
EL1007.fix: Use the receiver's agreed profile. If basic is required, correct the generator to emit permitted characters; if extended is accepted, use the default extended profile.
EL1007.false_positives: The basic profile is opt-in. A file accepted under the extended profile can trigger this warning when checked with --charset basic.

EL1008.fix: Replace the unintended character at the source with the intended permitted value. Verify ISA separator declarations before editing characters used structurally.
EL1008.false_positives: A caret is allowed when ISA11 declares it as the repetition separator. A partner-specific character agreement may differ from this profile; document that agreement before overriding the rule.

EL2001.fix: Choose the receiver's required record terminator and export it consistently. edilint fix normalizes to the dominant observed style; review the diff before writing.
EL2001.false_positives: A receiver may tolerate mixed endings, but other tools may not. The majority style is not proof of the intended style, especially for short files.

EL2002.fix: Append the agreed final record terminator. edilint fix can add it when the existing records establish a style.
EL2002.false_positives: Some line-oriented formats permit an unterminated final record. This is a warning; suppress it if the consumer's contract permits that form.

EL2003.example: An ISA declares ~ as the segment terminator, but the file ends with IEA*1*000000001 and no ~.
EL2003.fix: Check for truncation and regenerate missing data first. If only the final terminator is missing, preview edilint fix; it can append the declared terminator.
EL2003.false_positives: Incorrect ISA separator declarations can make otherwise visible terminators look missing. Check ISA before assuming the last byte is the only problem.

EL2004.fix: Use edilint fmt for consistent segment-per-line output, or preview edilint fix to normalize padding to the dominant style.
EL2004.false_positives: Many X12 readers ignore inter-segment whitespace. This warning catches inconsistent serialization; the majority style may not be the partner's required style.

EL2005.example: ISA declares * as both the element separator and the component separator.
EL2005.fix: Regenerate the interchange with distinct, non-alphanumeric separators and ensure the body uses those declarations. Editing only ISA can change how existing data is parsed.
EL2005.false_positives: A malformed or incorrectly padded ISA can shift separator positions and cause this secondary finding. Correct the ISA structure first.

EL2006.example: UNZ+1+EXAMPLE  (end of file without the declared apostrophe terminator)
EL2006.fix: Check for truncation. Restore the complete export, or append the active segment terminator if that is the only missing byte. Respect the UNA release character.
EL2006.false_positives: A malformed UNA declaration or a released apostrophe can change where a segment ends. Verify the service string before editing terminators.

EL3001.example: ISA*00*~  (far shorter than the fixed ISA envelope header)
EL3001.fix: Regenerate ISA with the required fixed-width fields and separators. Do not trim its space-padded fields. Remove a leading BOM if one displaced the header.
EL3001.false_positives: Forcing --type x12 on a non-X12 file also triggers this rule. Confirm format detection before repairing the input.

EL3002.fix: Restore the missing parent envelope or correct segment ordering in the exporter. Ensure GS is inside ISA and ST is inside GS.
EL3002.false_positives: An extracted transaction fragment lacks its parent envelopes. Lint the complete interchange when checking envelope integrity.

EL3003.example: ISA*...~GS*...~ST*835*0001~  (file ends before SE, GE, and IEA)
EL3003.fix: Recover the full export and restore matching trailers with correct counts and control numbers. Do not fabricate trailers if payload may have been truncated.
EL3003.false_positives: A deliberate partial interchange or a missing segment terminator can look unclosed. Check file completeness and terminators first.

EL3004.example: SE*2*0001~  (no preceding ST in the active group)
EL3004.fix: Restore the corresponding header or remove an unintended duplicate trailer at the source. Recheck nesting after repairing the file.
EL3004.false_positives: A fragment starting in the middle of an interchange can contain a trailer without its header. Use the full interchange for this check.

EL3005.fix: Make each trailer reference its actual header: ST02/SE02, GS06/GE02, and ISA13/IEA02. Determine the correct value from the source; do not guess between conflicting identifiers.
EL3005.false_positives: Pairs differing only in leading zeros are warnings. Some receivers compare numerically, while others require exact text, so confirm the contract before accepting the difference.

EL3006.fix: Count every segment from ST through SE, including both. Preview edilint fix to replace SE01 with the observed count after confirming the transaction is complete.
EL3006.false_positives: A missing terminator can merge segments and change the observed count. Fix segmentation first. A recount cannot prove that no payload was lost.

EL3007.example: A GS contains one ST/SE transaction set but ends with GE*2*1~.
EL3007.fix: Set GE01 to the number of transaction sets in that group. Preview edilint fix after checking that all intended transactions are present.
EL3007.false_positives: Broken transaction nesting can distort the recount. Repair structural findings before trusting a replacement count.

EL3008.example: An ISA contains one GS/GE group but ends with IEA*2*000000001~.
EL3008.fix: Set IEA01 to the number of functional groups in that interchange. Preview edilint fix after confirming the export is complete.
EL3008.false_positives: Malformed or missing group headers can affect the observed total. A corrected count alone does not establish that the file contains every intended group.

EL3009.example: Two interchanges in the same run both use ISA13 = 000000001.
EL3009.fix: Assign unique interchange controls, group controls within each interchange, and transaction controls within each group. Update matching trailers together.
EL3009.false_positives: Linting an original and its intentional retransmission together can report a duplicate ISA13. Run those files separately if duplicate detection is not intended across them.

EL3010.fix: Emit valid envelope dates and times in their required widths. edilint fix can zero-pad selected short times, but invalid calendar values must be corrected from the source.
EL3010.false_positives: Partner-specific shorthand is still nonconforming to the checked envelope representation. Dates are checked structurally, not for business plausibility or freshness.

EL3011.example: ISA13 is empty or contains only spaces.
EL3011.fix: Populate the interchange control number from the sender's control sequence and use the same value in IEA02.
EL3011.false_positives: A shifted or short ISA can make the control field appear empty. Repair ISA length and separators before assigning a new control value.

EL3012.fix: Move the extra segment into its intended transaction or remove an accidental suffix in the exporting system. Keep complete interchanges bounded by ISA and IEA.
EL3012.false_positives: A transport wrapper appended outside X12 can trigger this rule. Remove the transport framing before linting the EDI payload.

EL4001.example:
With --count-rule TRL:2:DTL:
DTL|EXAMPLE
TRL|2
(one DTL record, declared as two)
EL4001.fix: Verify the count rule's declaring field, counted record types, and scope. Then correct the exporter or declared total to match the intended records.
EL4001.false_positives: A wrong count-rule expression can count a different population than the sender intended. Explicitly define whether headers, trailers, and other record types belong in the total.

EL4002.fix: Write an integer in the declared count field, or correct the count rule if it points at a label rather than the count.
EL4002.false_positives: The configured field index or delimiter may be wrong. Check how the record was split before replacing the value.

EL4003.fix: Supply the missing declaring field or correct the configured count-field index. Field indexes are 1-based, so the record type occupies field 1.
EL4003.false_positives: An incorrect delimiter, record-type field, or count index can make a present field look missing. Verify the layout against the rule expression.

EL4004.example: With --count-rule TRL:2:DTL, the file contains DTL records but no TRL record.
EL4004.fix: Restore the declaring record if the feed requires it. Otherwise remove the count assertion or use the actual declaring record type.
EL4004.false_positives: A count rule shared across feeds can name a trailer that some feeds do not have. This warning means that the assertion was not checked, not that a total was proved incorrect.

EL4101.example:
DTL|A|1
DTL|B|2
DTL|C
(the last DTL has fewer fields)
EL4101.fix: Restore missing delimiters or fields, or remove an unintended delimiter in data. Compare records of the same type and verify the configured type field.
EL4101.false_positives: Optional trailing fields and variable-length record types can be intentional. HL7v2 findings are warnings for this reason. Disable or downgrade this heuristic for known variable layouts.

EL5001.example: A layout declares field widths 3 and 5, but the record contains only seven bytes.
EL5001.fix: Regenerate each record at the total width declared by its layout, padding each field as specified. Check that the supplied layout describes this feed version.
EL5001.false_positives: A stale layout can report valid data. Widths are measured in bytes, so multibyte UTF-8 characters occupy more than one position. Confirm that the layout describes this feed before adding padding.

EL5002.example: A width-5, right-aligned, space-padded field contains "AB   " instead of "   AB".
EL5002.fix: Apply padding on the side opposite the field's declared alignment. Fix the generator or update the layout if the alignment declaration is incorrect.
EL5002.false_positives: Only unambiguous opposite-side padding is reported. Significant leading or trailing pad characters may be data rather than padding; inspect the field's meaning before changing them.

EL6001.fix: Restore the complete batch or file envelope, including BTS for BHS and FTS for FHS. Confirm completeness before recounting trailers.
EL6001.false_positives: Bare MSH message streams are valid without batch headers. This pairing rule applies when envelope segments are present; partial captures may omit the closing segment.

EL6002.fix: Restore the missing envelope header or remove an accidental extra trailer. Keep each BTS inside its corresponding BHS batch and each FTS paired with FHS.
EL6002.false_positives: A capture starting midway through a batch may lack the header. Check the complete file before changing the sender.

EL6003.example: BHS|^~\&MSH|^~\&|EXAMPLEBTS|2  (one MSH, declared as two)
EL6003.fix: Count MSH messages in the batch and write that number to BTS-1. Preview edilint fix after verifying that no messages were lost.
EL6003.false_positives: Empty BTS-1 is optional and is not checked. Malformed batch structure can affect the recount; fix envelope errors first.

EL6004.example: FHS|^~\&BHS|^~\&BTS|0FTS|2  (one batch, declared as two)
EL6004.fix: Count BHS batches in the file and write that number to FTS-1. Preview edilint fix after confirming the file contains all intended batches.
EL6004.false_positives: Empty FTS-1 is optional and is not checked. A count change cannot recover a batch missing from a truncated export.

EL6005.example: BHS|^~\&MSH*^~\&*EXAMPLE  (field separator changes from | to *)
EL6005.fix: Use consistent declared separators and well-formed encoding characters throughout each enclosing batch/file context. Regenerate payload fields with the same declarations.
EL6005.false_positives: Separately valid messages concatenated under one batch header may disagree. Validate them separately or normalize their serialization before batching; changing only the header is insufficient.

EL6006.example: BHS|^~\&BTS|0MSH|^~\&|EXAMPLE  (message is outside the closed batch)
EL6006.fix: Place the message inside its intended BHS/BTS batch and update the trailer count, or export a bare message stream if batching is not intended.
EL6006.false_positives: Bare message streams without BHS are not checked for stray messages. A feed intentionally mixing batched and bare messages may need a documented exception.

EL7001.example: UNH+1+INVOIC:D:96A:UN'  (inside UNB, but no UNT follows)
EL7001.fix: Restore the matching UNT, UNE, and UNZ trailers for open headers after confirming the export is complete. Recheck counts and control references.
EL7001.false_positives: Message fragments and incomplete captures can lack closing envelopes. A bad service string or terminator can also hide an otherwise present trailer.

EL7002.fix: Restore the missing header or remove an unintended duplicate trailer at the source. Check UNH/UNT, UNG/UNE, and UNB/UNZ pairing.
EL7002.false_positives: A fragment extracted from the middle of a message can start with an unmatched trailer. Check the full interchange.

EL7003.fix: Count segments from UNH through UNT inclusive and correct UNT-1 after confirming message completeness. Released terminators inside data do not end segments.
EL7003.false_positives: Malformed release sequences or missing terminators can affect the observed count. Resolve tokenizer and service-string findings before recounting.

EL7004.example: A UNG contains one UNH/UNT message but ends with UNE+2+GROUP1'.
EL7004.fix: Set UNE-1 to the number of messages in that functional group after checking that all intended messages are present.
EL7004.false_positives: Bad nesting or missing message headers can change the observed total. A corrected trailer count does not prove payload completeness.

EL7005.example: An ungrouped UNB contains one message but ends with UNZ+2+EXAMPLE'.
EL7005.fix: Set UNZ-1 to the number of messages in an ungrouped interchange, or to the number of functional groups when UNG groups are used.
EL7005.false_positives: Counting messages instead of groups in a grouped interchange causes a mismatch. Confirm the envelope form before changing the trailer.

EL7006.fix: Match UNH-1/UNT-2, UNG-5/UNE-2, and UNB-5/UNZ-2 exactly. Fill empty header references from the source's control sequence.
EL7006.false_positives: Numerically equal references with different leading zeros are warnings. A receiver may compare text exactly, so do not assume numeric equality is sufficient.

EL7007.example: UNA++.? '  (component and element separators both use +)
EL7007.fix: Emit a nine-character UNA with distinct permitted service characters and a period or comma decimal mark. Ensure the payload uses those declarations.
EL7007.false_positives: Truncated or incorrectly decoded UNA bytes can create secondary separator errors. Verify the original export before rewriting the service string.

EL7008.fix: Place messages and groups inside the required interchange envelope, or lint the complete interchange instead of a standalone fragment.
EL7008.false_positives: Forcing --type edifact on another format, or checking only an extracted message, can trigger missing-envelope findings. Confirm the input scope and format.

EL7009.fix: Remove an accidental transport suffix or place the segment inside its intended message. Keep all EDIFACT segments inside an interchange.
EL7009.false_positives: Transport framing outside the interchange may be deliberate. Strip the wrapper and lint only the EDI payload.
